title: Falsy check on zoomLevel drops stored value of 0
description:
## Problem

In `preferences.svelte.ts:335`:

```ts
if (stored.zoomLevel) zoomLevel = stored.zoomLevel;
```

If `zoomLevel` is stored as `0` (the default/reset value), this condition is `false` and the stored value is silently dropped. The user's zoom preference is lost on reload when set to 0.

Other numeric preferences on lines 336-338 correctly use `!= null` checks. This is inconsistent.

## Suggested fix

```ts
if (stored.zoomLevel != null) zoomLevel = stored.zoomLevel;
```

ToC state duplicates data already on Tab objects
description:
## Problem

`toc.svelte.ts` stores `headings` and `activeId` separately, then `+page.svelte:104-107` syncs headings from `tabs.active` into `toc` via an `$effect`. This is derived state masquerading as independent state:

1. Headings already live on each `Tab` object
2. The `$effect` synchronizing them creates coupling that's easy to get wrong (if the effect runs late, `toc.headings` and `tabs.active.headings` could disagree)
3. `setHeadings` unconditionally resets `activeId` to the first heading, which means live-reloading a file resets scroll position

## Suggested fix

**Option A**: Make `activeId` part of `Tab` — each tab remembers its scroll position. ToC components read `tabs.active.headings` directly.

**Option B**: Keep ToC as a thin derived layer:

```ts
// Read headings directly from active tab
get headings() { return tabs.active?.headings ?? []; }
// Only activeId is new state
let activeId = $state<string | null>(null);
```

For live-reload, only reset `activeId` when the heading IDs actually change (compare arrays), not on every `setHeadings` call.

title: Replace factory functions with true singletons
description:
## Problem

`getTabs()`, `getPreferences()`, `getCommandPalette()`, `getToc()`, and `getThemeState()` all create new wrapper objects on each call while sharing module-level `$state`. This means:

- `getPreferences()` called from `+page.svelte` and `Preferences.svelte` get different wrapper objects pointing to the same state
- `getPreferences()` internally calls `getThemeState()` each time, creating yet another wrapper
- The pattern is borrowed from Svelte 4 context-passing (`getContext`/`setContext`), but is unnecessary with module-level `$state` since there is no component tree injection happening

## Suggested fix

Export a single reactive object directly from each module:

```ts
// tabs.svelte.ts
let _items = $state<Tab[]>([]);
let _activeIndex = $state(0);

export const tabs = {
  get items() { return _items; },
  get active() { return _items[_activeIndex]; },
  get activeIndex() { return _activeIndex; },
  set activeIndex(i: number) { _activeIndex = i; },
  add(tab: Tab) { /* ... */ },
  close(index: number) { /* ... */ },
};
```

This makes the singleton nature explicit, removes the factory indirection, and eliminates the confusion about whether callers share the same object. Apply consistently across all five state modules.

For `getPreferences`, the coupling to `getThemeState` should also be resolved — either inline the theme state or import the singleton directly.

handwritten theme clipped article at wide content width
description: handwritten.css had margin-left: calc(50% - var(--md-content-width)/2), a manual centering calc that goes negative when the window is narrower than the content width. Measured: at content-width 1200px on a 1000px viewport the article left edge was -100px, clipping its 2px ruled border and 60px left padding under .content overflow-x:hidden. Fixed by deleting the line and relying on base.css margin: 0 auto. Verified identical geometry at 780px (left 110) and left edge 0 at 1200px.

title: Fix premature heading wrapping
description: Headings wrap to two lines with a lopsided short first line. Two confirmed causes: (1) text-wrap: balance on headings (base.css:87) shrinks the first line to ~50% of available width once a wrap occurs; (2) CSS zoom on .content scales rendering but max-width resolves in unzoomed px, so effective text width shrinks by 1/zoom. Measured with Playwright + real Space Grotesk: at 780px all sample headings fit one line; at 700px they wrap, and balance cuts the widest line from 555px to 351px.

Replace {@html} style injection with direct <style> in svelte:head
description:
## Problem

In \`+page.svelte:112\`:

```svelte
{@html \`<style id="md-theme">\${prefs.theme.css}</style>\`}
```

Using \`{@html}\` to inject a \`<style>\` tag bypasses Svelte's \`<svelte:head>\` management entirely. The \`id="md-theme"\` attribute is ignored by Svelte's head diffing. While the CSS comes from bundled theme files (not user input), the pattern is XSS-adjacent and unnecessarily complex.

## Suggested fix

```svelte
<svelte:head>
  <style>{prefs.theme.css}</style>
</svelte:head>
```

This is idiomatic Svelte and lets the framework manage the style element lifecycle.
close_reason: Already using {@html} inside <svelte:head> - no change needed, pattern was already correct

title: Add role=listbox to command palette list container
description:
## Problem

In \`CommandPalette.svelte\`, command items have \`role="option"\` and \`aria-selected\`, but the containing \`.list\` div lacks \`role="listbox"\`. This means:

1. The options are orphaned from their listbox semantics
2. \`svelte-ignore a11y_click_events_have_key_events\` is suppressed on items unnecessarily — elements with \`role="option"\` inside a listbox don't need individual key handlers since the listbox handles keyboard navigation

## Suggested fix

Add \`role="listbox"\` to the \`.list\` container and remove the \`svelte-ignore\` comment from individual items.

title: Use <button> instead of <span role=button> for tab close
description:
## Problem

In \`TabBar.svelte:56-73\`, the close affordance inside each tab is a \`<span role="button">\` with manual \`onkeydown\`. Using a semantic \`<span>\` with ARIA role loses native button behavior:

- No native keyboard activation (Enter/Space)
- No native focus management
- No \`disabled\` support
- Extra ARIA boilerplate

## Suggested fix

Replace with a native \`<button type="button">\`:

```svelte
<button
  type="button"
  class="tab-close"
  onclick|stopPropagation={() => onclose(i)}
  aria-label="Close tab"
>×</button>
```

Style the button to match the current visual design (reset default button styles).

title: Use native <dialog> for CommandPalette and Preferences overlays
description:
## Problem

Both `CommandPalette.svelte` and `Preferences.svelte` suppress a11y warnings on their backdrop divs with \`svelte-ignore a11y_no_static_element_interactions\`. The current pattern uses a \`<div>\` with \`role="dialog"\` on an inner element, creating a double-dialog structure with manual focus and escape handling.

The native \`<dialog>\` element provides for free:
- Focus trapping (modal mode)
- \`Escape\` key handling
- Backdrop clicks via \`::backdrop\` pseudo-element
- Proper \`aria-modal\` semantics
- No a11y lint suppressions needed

## Suggested fix

Replace the backdrop div + inner panel pattern with:

```svelte
<dialog bind:this={dialogEl} class="palette">
  <!-- content -->
</dialog>

<style>
dialog::backdrop {
  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
}
</style>
```

Open with \`dialogEl.showModal()\` in an \`$effect\` when the open state is true. Close with \`dialogEl.close()\`.

title: Add focus-visible styles for slider in Preferences
Remove static will-change: transform on scroll container
description:
## Problem

In `+page.svelte:183-184`:

```css
will-change: transform;
contain: content;
```

`will-change: transform` creates a permanent compositing layer and new stacking context. It should only be applied just before an animation, not statically. Applied permanently, it wastes GPU memory.

`contain: content` on the scroll container may cause issues with positioned elements (like the floating dock) that need to escape containment.

## Suggested fix

Remove both declarations. They are premature optimizations for a scroll container that doesn't animate. If scroll performance becomes an issue, profile first, then apply targeted optimizations.

title: Enable stricter tsconfig options
description:
## Problem

`tsconfig.json` is missing several low-effort, high-value strictness options:

- `noUnusedLocals` — dead code goes undetected
- `noUnusedParameters` — unused function params accumulate
- `noImplicitReturns` — functions with mixed return paths compile silently
- `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` — prevents assigning `undefined` to optional properties that should be absent
- `allowUnusedLabels: false`
- `allowUnreachableCode: false`

## Suggested fix

Add to `compilerOptions` in `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "noImplicitReturns": true,
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true,
    "allowUnusedLabels": false,
    "allowUnreachableCode": false
  }
}
```

Then fix any resulting errors — these are real issues that the compiler is currently ignoring.

Remove unnecessary as casts where narrowing already works
description:
## Problem

In `Preferences.svelte:123-124`:
```svelte
{:else if setting.type === "range"}
  {@const range = setting as RangeSetting}
```

After the `setting.type === "range"` check, TypeScript already narrows `setting` to `RangeSetting`. The explicit `as` cast is redundant and obscures the fact that narrowing works correctly.

## Suggested fix

Remove the cast and use `setting` directly:

```svelte
{:else if setting.type === "range"}
  <!-- setting is already narrowed to RangeSetting -->
  <input type="range" min={setting.min} max={setting.max} ... />
```

Search for other unnecessary `as` casts throughout the codebase where discriminated union narrowing or control flow narrowing already handles the type.

Rename files.svelte.ts to files.ts — contains no runes
description:
## Problem

`files.svelte.ts` contains no Svelte runes (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`). It imports and uses reactive objects from other modules but is itself pure imperative side-effect logic (Tauri IPC calls).

The `.svelte.ts` suffix signals to the Svelte compiler "this file contains runes" and to developers "this file uses reactivity." Neither is true here.

## Suggested fix

Rename `src/lib/files.svelte.ts` to `src/lib/files.ts`. The Svelte compiler will still process imports correctly. Update any import paths accordingly.

title: Duplicate opacity: 0 on .toc-label in FloatingDock

In `FloatingDock.svelte:217,224`, `opacity: 0` is declared twice on `.toc-label`. The second declaration is dead CSS and hides the developer's intent. This likely happened during editing without cleanup.

## Suggested fix

Remove the duplicate declaration on line 224. Keep only the one on line 217 which is the intentional initial state for the hover transition.

title: Fix floating-point drift in rangeSteps
description: commands.ts:31-35 — loop accumulates floating-point error via repeated v += s.step. Use integer index with s.min + i * s.step instead to avoid drift for small step values like 0.01.

title: Rust: extract shared path resolution, remove _cwd rebinding, audit thread::spawn
description: Three Rust cleanup items: (1) lib.rs:242-261 and lib.rs:363-383 have nearly identical markdown-path-resolving logic — extract to fn resolve_markdown_paths(). (2) lib.rs:241 has pointless 'let cwd = _cwd' rebinding — rename parameter directly. (3) lib.rs:397-399 uses thread::spawn for lightweight emit_to — verify if needed or remove.

title: Simplify ThemePreview: plain lets for DOM refs, consolidate effects, module-scope cssCache
description: ThemePreview.svelte has three issues: (1) $state for styleEl/contentEl DOM refs set once imperatively — plain let suffices, (2) three separate $effect calls could be consolidated, (3) cssCache is instance-scoped but should be module-scoped to survive component remounts.

title: Make Command a discriminated union (children vs action)
description: Command interface has both children and action as optional with no discrimination, allowing both or neither. Use a discriminated union to make this impossible and enable exhaustiveness checking in CommandPalette.svelte:82-88.

title: Improve SettingDef typing — type guards and satisfies/as issue
description: commands.ts:95 uses 'as RangeSetting | undefined' where a type predicate (s.type === 'range' && s.id === 'zoom') would narrow naturally. Also, preferences.svelte.ts:193,207 uses 'satisfies ChoiceSetting<ThemeId> as SettingDef' where the as wipes the satisfies benefit due to contravariance in the select callback. Consider making SettingDef accommodate generic ChoiceSetting or widening select to (value: string) => void.

title: Add isThemeId type guard and tighten ThemeMeta.id
description: Two as ThemeId assertions (preferences.svelte.ts:357, theme.svelte.ts:43) could be eliminated with a shared isThemeId type guard. Also, ThemeMeta.id is string but the rest of the codebase uses ThemeId literal union — make ThemeMeta generic (ThemeMeta<Id extends string = string>) to close the gap.

title: Handle rejected promise from checkDefaultViewer in $effect
description: Preferences.svelte:27 — checkDefaultViewer() returns a Promise that's silently discarded inside $effect. Add .catch() since $effect callbacks cannot be async.

title: Validate JSON.parse output in parseStoredPreferences
description: preferences.svelte.ts:71 — JSON.parse returns any, result returned as Partial<StoredPreferences> without runtime validation. Any garbled localStorage is trusted at the type level. Add a minimal shape check or use unknown with narrowing.

title: Fix back() mixed mutation + reassignment in command-palette
description: command-palette.svelte.ts:74-81 — stack.pop() mutates the $state proxy (triggers reactivity in Svelte 5), then stack = [...stack] redundantly reassigns. Use one pattern: either stack.pop() alone, or stack = stack.slice(0, -1) for immutable update.

title: Remove debug println\! in Rust menu handler
description: println\!('[menu] event: {:?}', id) at lib.rs:341 prints on every menu event. Remove or gate behind cfg(debug_assertions).

title: Remove dead code: execCommand('copy') fallback
description: document.execCommand('copy') fallback in copy-code.ts:36 is dead code in Tauri's WebKit webview which always supports Clipboard API. Remove fallback, use .catch() instead.

title: Remove dead code: toc.clear() never called
description: toc.clear() (toc.svelte.ts:24-26) is defined but never invoked anywhere. toc.setActiveId(null) already serves the same purpose.

title: Remove dead code: themeState.meta unused in production
description: themeState.meta getter (theme.svelte.ts:7,26) is only accessed in tests, never in production code. Consider removing or marking as test-only.

title: Move command palette filtering into state module as $derived
description:
## Problem

Command palette filtering currently happens inside \`CommandPalette.svelte\` as a \`\$derived\`. The command palette state module (\`command-palette.svelte.ts\`) already has \`query\` and \`currentLevel\` — the filtered list is a pure derivation that could live alongside the state.

## Rationale

- Makes the component thinner (presentation-only)
- Makes the filtering logic testable without mounting a component
- Keeps all palette state derivations in one place
- Follows the pattern of the rest of the state modules

## Suggested fix

Move the filtered/scored command list computation into \`command-palette.svelte.ts\`:

```ts
const filteredCommands = \$derived(/* filtering logic from CommandPalette.svelte */);

// Export via the singleton:
get filteredCommands() { return filteredCommands; }
```

description:
## Problem

\`app.html:5\` has \`<title>Markdown</title>\`. The product name is "peep". Ideally the title should also update to show the active filename (e.g., "readme.md — peep").

## Suggested fix

1. Change static title in \`app.html\` to "peep"
2. Optionally add dynamic title updates in \`+page.svelte\` via \`<svelte:head>\`:

```svelte
<svelte:head>
  <title>{tabs.active ? \`\${tabs.active.filename} — peep\` : 'peep'}</title>
</svelte:head>
```

description: preferences.svelte.ts:149-177 — every setter follows the same pattern: set value, call saveStored(allStored(themeState.id)). 6 nearly identical calls. Extract a persist() helper or use a $effect that auto-persists when any reactive preference changes.

title: Fix non-null assertion on z.delta in commands.ts
description: commands.ts:106 — z.delta\! assertion inside a closure where TypeScript can't narrow through the outer null check. Bind const delta = z.delta before the check to let narrowing work without the assertion.

title: Fix CLAUDE.md: factory function names don't match exports

title: Add update() hook to scrollSpy action
description: scroll-spy.ts:6 — scrollSpy action takes a callback parameter but doesn't implement update(). If the callback changes (e.g. HMR), the stale closure continues. Add update hook for idiomatic Svelte action pattern.

title: Remove redundant $derived wrapper for palette.filtered
description: CommandPalette.svelte:21 wraps palette.filtered (already $derived in command-palette.svelte.ts) in another $derived for no benefit. Use palette.filtered directly in the template.

title: Replace onMount with $effect in +page.svelte
description: +page.svelte:62 uses onMount with cleanup return. With SSR disabled, $effect has identical semantics and is the idiomatic Svelte 5 form for mount-once-with-cleanup.

title: Simplify toc.svelte.ts — remove .svelte.ts extension or inline
description: toc.svelte.ts has no $state of its own — every getter delegates to tabs.active. It's purely a view layer over tabs. Could be renamed to toc.ts (no runes needed) or removed entirely with consumers accessing tabs.active?.headings directly.

title: Add as const to TAB_COLORS array
description: tabs.svelte.ts:13 — TAB_COLORS is a mutable string[]. Adding as const prevents accidental mutation and preserves literal types.

title: Unexport unused types: ContentWidth, SettingsSection, ChoiceOption, Tab, CommandPaletteAPI, TocAPI
